---
title: "Recipe 12 — Verify a release: the SLSA provenance check before you deploy"
---

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`gh attestation`](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify) · [`release-attest.yml`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-attest.yml) | Supply chain | easy | 3 min | release | SLSA, attestation, supply-chain, TR-81 |

### Problem

You downloaded a Trishula release asset. You want proof of what built it:
which workflow, from which commit, signed by whom. You want that proof
before the binary runs anywhere.

### Solution

Every release asset carries two attestations the moment the release
publishes: the SLSA provenance (`https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`) and the
SPDX SBOM (`https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3`). Both are Rekor-backed
Sigstore bundles.

1. Verify one asset:

```bash
gh attestation verify trishula-engine-linux-arm64 -R trishula-dev/trishula
```

2. Read what a bundle states. The attestation API returns the full
   envelope per digest; the provenance names the builder and the run:

```text
builder.id  = https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/.github/workflows/release-attest.yml@refs/heads/main
buildType   = https://actions.github.io/buildtypes/workflow/v1
invocation  = https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/actions/runs/<run-id>
```

3. Check the count matches the release. The rc3 asset
   `ban_enforce_arm64_bpfel.o` (sha256 `cad16bcf…`) carried 6 provenance
   + 6 SBOM bundles (the attest runs re-run per re-attest; every bundle
   verifies independently).

4. Verify in bulk before deploying a fleet:

```bash
gh release download <tag> -R trishula-dev/trishula -D assets
for f in assets/*; do gh attestation verify "$f" -R trishula-dev/trishula; done
```

### Discussion

The verification runs offline-grade: the bundle carries the Rekor
inclusion promise and proof; `gh attestation verify` checks the Sigstore
trust root. A failed verify = the asset does not match what CI built —
do not deploy it, file it. The SHA in `checksums.txt` pins the bytes;
the attestation pins the producer. Both must hold.

The GA cut notes carry this block per the release rule; the verify
command runs the same on every future tag.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@97206190](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/97206190ed003e5eea8d62aeb750e42545f99c83)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25:

- `gh attestation verify /tmp/ban_enforce_arm64_bpfel.o -R trishula-dev/trishula`
  on the `2026.01-rc3` asset: exit 0.
- The attestation API read 12 bundles for the asset sha: 6 provenance/v1
  + 6 SPDX 2.3; the builder id, the build type and the Rekor log entries
  recorded above.
